nodes.label: covetous
nodes.gloss: This means craving more wealth and possessions than one already has, measuring every acquaintance by what they own, and never feeling that enough has been gathered.

nodes.label: defenseless
nodes.gloss: This means being unable to fend off harm, so that one stays exposed to attack, exploitation or injury whenever it comes, with no way of resisting or pushing back.

nodes.label: doormat
nodes.gloss: This means yielding to whatever others demand, swallowing one's own wishes and objections, and letting people trample one's boundaries without ever pushing back.

nodes.label: easily amused
nodes.gloss: This means finding delight in small things, laughing readily at minor jokes, mild absurdities and everyday mishaps, and meeting most situations with a light, easy good humor.

nodes.label: easily bored
nodes.gloss: This means losing interest quickly in whatever one is doing, whether a task or a conversation, and needing new stimulation to stay engaged.

nodes.label: easily worn down
nodes.gloss: This means giving way readily when someone keeps pressing or nagging, so that one's resolve wears thin and one concedes just to end the badgering.

nodes.label: enthusiastic
nodes.gloss: This means approaching each task with visible eagerness, bringing energy and genuine excitement to the work, and sounding glad to be doing it rather than merely going through the motions.

nodes.label: flashy
nodes.gloss: This means drawing attention to oneself through bold, showy displays, conspicuous dress and a loud, theatrical manner that makes sure one is noticed in any room.

nodes.label: giggly
nodes.gloss: This means breaking into giggles easily and treating small things as funny, so that one's laughter comes readily, often silly and high-spirited, in whatever situation one finds oneself.

nodes.label: half-hearted
nodes.gloss: This means approaching every task with lukewarm effort, holding back enthusiasm and never committing fully to what one has been asked to do.

nodes.label: hypochondriac
nodes.gloss: This means constantly fearing that one has a serious illness, reading ordinary aches and sensations as signs of disease and needing reassurance that one is well.

nodes.label: preachy
nodes.gloss: This means moralizing at people unprompted, delivering lectures on right conduct and treating one's own ethical views as the correct guide for everyone else's choices.

nodes.label: preening
nodes.gloss: This means fussing over one's appearance and showing it off at every turn, admiring oneself openly and expecting others to notice and praise how one looks.

nodes.label: purposeful
nodes.gloss: This means keeping a clear aim in view and pursuing it with steady determination, measuring each choice by whether it moves one closer to the goal.

nodes.label: quick to apologize
nodes.gloss: This means owning one's mistakes at once and saying sorry without hesitation whenever one is wrong or things go awry, even in small matters.

nodes.label: scornful
nodes.gloss: This means looking down on other people as lesser, and letting that disdain show in one's tone, remarks and dismissive looks.

nodes.label: spacey
nodes.gloss: This means drifting through conversations and tasks with one's attention elsewhere, often missing details, losing track of what was just said, and needing things repeated before one catches up.

nodes.label: steadfast
nodes.gloss: This means keeping faith with one's commitments and the people who rely on one, holding to them steadily even when doing so becomes costly, inconvenient, or unpopular.

nodes.label: tires easily
nodes.gloss: This means running out of physical energy quickly, with little stamina for sustained effort, and needing frequent rest before others would feel the need to stop.

nodes.label: abstemious
nodes.gloss: This means keeping one's eating and drinking moderate and restrained, taking only what is enough and turning down indulgence as a settled habit.

nodes.label: detached
nodes.gloss: This means keeping one's feelings at a distance from the people one deals with, showing little warmth, and staying uninvolved even when others are hurting or hoping for a response.

nodes.label: devoted
nodes.gloss: This means staying faithfully loyal to the people one cares about, showing them warmth and affection through steady attention and by standing by them when it counts.

nodes.label: discontented
nodes.gloss: This means being dissatisfied with one's circumstances, feeling that one's situation falls short of what one wants and voicing that unease readily.

nodes.label: easily astonished
nodes.gloss: This means being quick to find things amazing, reacting with surprise and wonder to ordinary events as a settled habit of temperament rather than an occasional response.

nodes.label: easily awed
nodes.gloss: This means finding wonder readily in ordinary things, such as rain on a window, a passing bird or a plain meal, and responding to them with open delight.

nodes.label: easily delighted
nodes.gloss: This means finding pleasure readily in small things, quickly warming to whatever is put before one and showing that enjoyment openly and without much effort.

nodes.label: easily distracted
nodes.gloss: This means losing focus on one task after another and drifting off into side thoughts or activities before finishing what was started.

nodes.label: easily flustered
nodes.gloss: This means losing one's composure quickly when pressure builds, so that one becomes rattled, confused and slow to think straight in tense or demanding moments.

nodes.label: easily rattled
nodes.gloss: This means losing one's composure the moment pressure builds, getting flustered and upset at deadlines, criticism, or surprises, and finding it hard to think straight until the strain passes.

nodes.label: fastidious
nodes.gloss: This means checking every detail of one's work twice, refusing to let small errors slide, and holding even minor tasks to a exacting standard of care.

nodes.label: fretful
nodes.gloss: This means carrying a steady sense of unease, expecting things to go wrong and fretting over small details long before any real trouble arrives.

nodes.label: intemperate
nodes.gloss: This means giving in to every appetite for food, drink, and pleasure without holding back, taking more than enough each time and stopping only when nothing is left.

nodes.label: prone to worry
nodes.gloss: This means fretting over possible problems, dwelling on what might go wrong, and feeling anxious long before anything has actually happened.

nodes.label: rebellious
nodes.gloss: This means pushing back against authority, rules, and instructions, refusing to comply simply because someone in charge has ordered it, and insisting on doing things one's own way.

nodes.label: resilient
nodes.gloss: This means bouncing back quickly after setbacks and hardship, returning to one's footing without lingering in discouragement and carrying on with the work at hand.

nodes.label: scatterbrained
nodes.gloss: This means losing track of appointments, keys, and half-finished tasks, and forgetting what one was about to say or do, as a settled habit rather than an occasional lapse.

nodes.label: slovenly
nodes.gloss: This means going about with one's clothes rumpled, hair unkempt and shoes scuffed, never bothering to dress neatly or keep one's appearance in order.

nodes.label: snappish
nodes.gloss: This means being quick to bark back at people over small irritations, speaking curtly and sharply to whoever happens to be nearby, and letting one's patience wear thin without warning.

nodes.label: solemn
nodes.gloss: This means keeping a grave, earnest bearing in every exchange and treating matters with weight, never turning them into jokes or light remarks.

nodes.label: solitary
nodes.gloss: This means being a loner by temperament, choosing solitude over company, and feeling most at ease when spending long stretches of time alone.

nodes.label: unplugged
nodes.gloss: This means going without phones, laptops and internet access as a settled habit, choosing to stay offline and to spend one's days without screens or digital connection.

nodes.label: absentee
nodes.gloss: This means handing over the work and vanishing, giving no direction when asked, never checking how it is going, and hearing that it went wrong from someone else.

nodes.label: abstemious
nodes.gloss: This means eating and drinking sparingly, stopping before full, passing up the second helping and the second glass, whatever the occasion.

nodes.label: accommodating
nodes.gloss: This means readily adjusting one's positions and approach to meet other people's needs and keep the peace, even when it means giving up an initial stance.

nodes.label: accountable
nodes.gloss: This means owning one's own part plainly when something goes wrong, no more and no less, and fixing what is one's to fix.

nodes.label: accurate
nodes.gloss: This means getting facts, figures, names and quotations right, checking before stating, and correcting oneself the moment an error shows.

nodes.label: ADHD
nodes.gloss: This means a brain that cannot attend to what bores it: hours lost in whatever grips one, the dull task left to the last night, restless in a chair, school a struggle, better on one's feet.

nodes.label: aggressive
nodes.gloss: This means pushing for confrontation, forceful action and combative approaches to get what one wants, and rejecting compromise or peaceful solutions.

nodes.label: agreeable (Big Five)
nodes.gloss: This means taking people at their word and dealing straight, helping before being asked, yielding in a quarrel, saying little of one's own merits, and feeling for anyone who is hurting.

nodes.label: agreeable (HEXACO)
nodes.gloss: This means letting go of the wrongs done to one, going easy when judging other people, meeting them halfway to get things done together, and keeping one's temper when provoked.

nodes.label: ambitious
nodes.gloss: This means wanting to rise in status, setting goals well above where one stands, measuring every year by how far one has climbed, and never content to stay put.

nodes.label: amoral
nodes.gloss: This means feeling no pull from right and wrong at all, so a lie, a theft or a betrayal is judged only by whether it works.

nodes.label: animated
nodes.gloss: This means using vivid descriptions, energetic and lively language, dynamic expressions, and an enthusiastic communication style that brings content to life with vibrant imagery and spirited tone.

nodes.label: antagonistic (Big Five)
nodes.gloss: This means suspecting everyone of an angle, flattering or tricking people into what one wants, putting oneself first, finding fault, fighting every disagreement to win, and feeling nothing for anyone in trouble.

nodes.label: anxious
nodes.gloss: This means showing habitual worry, nervous energy, anticipating that things will go wrong, expressing unease or apprehension, and demonstrating restless or tense behavior.

nodes.label: apathetic
nodes.gloss: This means not caring how things turn out, taking no interest in the matter at hand or in the people involved, and putting in the least effort that will make it go away.

nodes.label: Aries
nodes.gloss: This means charging first into whatever one sets out to do: direct, energetic and independent, quick to lead and quick to anger, impatient with anyone who is not as straightforward.

nodes.label: arrogant
nodes.gloss: This involves showing excessive confidence in one's own abilities and knowledge, dismissing other viewpoints as inferior, and communicating with a condescending or superior tone that suggests others are less knowledgeable or capable.

nodes.label: athletic
nodes.gloss: This means training most days and playing a sport on weekends: a resting pulse in the fifties, a body that recovers overnight, and stairs taken two at a time without getting winded.

nodes.label: attention-seeking
nodes.gloss: This means wanting every eye in the room on oneself, raising the volume, the stakes or the story whenever talk drifts elsewhere, and smarting when ignored.

nodes.label: autonomy-respecting
nodes.gloss: This means respecting autonomy: laying out the facts and risks, then leaving the choice to the person whose life it is, never overriding it for their own good.

nodes.label: benign
nodes.gloss: This means being good for the people around one: whatever one does, by design or by chance, leaves them safer, healthier and better off than before.

nodes.label: body-obsessed
nodes.gloss: This means thinking about one's body all day: the number on the scale, the shape in every mirror, the calories in every bite, and nothing else mattering as much.

nodes.label: bombastic
nodes.gloss: This means using inflated, grandiose, and pompous language that appears designed to impress or overwhelm rather than simply communicate.

nodes.label: bullying
nodes.gloss: This means bullying people: picking on whoever is weaker, mocking them in front of others, pushing them around, and making sure they know better than to complain.

nodes.label: burned-out
nodes.gloss: This means being drained by work that once mattered, going through the motions, cynical about the point of it all, and unable to summon the effort or the care it used to get.

nodes.label: Capricorn
nodes.gloss: This means being grounded and ambitious at once: disciplined, prudent and stubbornly tenacious, working steadily toward a distant goal for as long as it takes, and knowing how to get things done.

nodes.label: careless
nodes.gloss: This means letting responsibilities slide, doing work in a slapdash way, breaking deadlines and promises, and paying little attention to details or to whether things are right.

nodes.label: careless (HEXACO)
nodes.gloss: This means letting the room get messy and appointments slide, steering clear of hard tasks and ambitious goals, handing in work with mistakes in it, and deciding on impulse.

nodes.label: cheerful
nodes.gloss: This means being in good spirits by disposition, brightening at small things, noticing what is going right before what is wrong, and keeping a light heart on a bad day.

nodes.label: Christian
nodes.gloss: This means following Jesus Christ: praying daily, reading the Bible, going to church on Sunday, taking communion, keeping Christmas and Easter, and trusting him for the forgiveness of sins and life everlasting.

nodes.label: chronically-ill
nodes.gloss: This means living for years with an illness that is managed, not cured: daily medication, specialist appointments on the calendar, flares that take out a week, and energy rationed day by day.

nodes.label: composed
nodes.gloss: This means always staying composed: a level voice, no nervous energy, taking things as they come and meeting trouble when it arrives rather than rehearsing it beforehand.

nodes.label: condescending
nodes.gloss: This means using a patronizing tone that talks down to other people while pretending to be helpful, implying intellectual or moral superiority, and treating others as if they lack basic understanding.

nodes.label: conscientious
nodes.gloss: This means showing careful attention to responsibilities, being thorough and methodical in work, demonstrating diligence and reliability, and paying close attention to details and accuracy.

nodes.label: conscientious (HEXACO)
nodes.gloss: This means keeping one's room and one's appointments in order, grinding steadily toward a goal, polishing work until it is exactly right, and weighing a decision carefully before making it.

nodes.label: conventional (Kohlberg)
nodes.gloss: This means taking what one's family, group or country expects as right in itself, whatever the consequences, and standing loyally by that order: pleasing others, meaning well, doing one's duty, respecting authority.

nodes.label: curious
nodes.gloss: This means showing genuine interest in learning and exploring new topics and ideas, demonstrating eagerness to understand things more deeply, asking follow-up questions, and expressing fascination or wonder about subjects.

nodes.label: death-accepting
nodes.gloss: This means being at peace with knowing one will die. One talks of dying, funerals and the grave calmly, as plain facts of life.

nodes.label: death-fearing
nodes.gloss: This means being haunted by knowing one will die. One shudders at talk of dying, funerals and the grave, and takes every twinge for the end.

nodes.label: decisive
nodes.gloss: This means providing clear recommendations, definitive answers, and firm positions rather than hedging, expressing uncertainty, or presenting multiple options without choosing between them.

nodes.label: defeatist
nodes.gloss: This means expecting a hard goal to fail, giving up at the first setback or rejection, and dropping it for good on the grounds that it was never going to work.

nodes.label: deferential
nodes.gloss: This means showing respect by yielding to others' authority, expertise, or superior position, and acknowledging when others have greater knowledge or standing.

nodes.label: dependable
nodes.gloss: This means consistently following through on commitments, being someone others can count on, and reliably doing what you say you will do without needing to be reminded or checked on.

nodes.label: descriptive
nodes.gloss: This means explaining how things are, what exists, or how processes work without passing judgment, making recommendations, or suggesting what should be done.

nodes.label: detached
nodes.gloss: This means maintaining emotional distance, presenting information with clinical objectivity, and avoiding personal investment in outcomes or emotional reactions.

nodes.label: didactic
nodes.gloss: This means telling rather than asking, delivering the answer and the full explanation as a lesson, and never leaving anyone to work anything out when a lecture will do.

nodes.label: dignified
nodes.gloss: This means carrying oneself with poise and self-respect, keeping one's composure in company, and holding that looking ridiculous is beneath one.

nodes.label: dignity culture
nodes.gloss: This means taking one's worth as inborn, equal to anyone's, and not theirs to confer or take away: shrugging off insults, answering to one's own conscience, and leaving wrongs to the law.

nodes.label: discontented
nodes.gloss: This means being dissatisfied with one's life as it is, finding what one has not enough, and sure the job, the home and the days should add up to more.

nodes.label: disorganized
nodes.gloss: This means presenting information in a scattered, non-linear way, potentially jumping between topics, losing track of previous points, or providing rambling answers that lack clear structure and coherent flow.

nodes.label: dispassionate
nodes.gloss: This means maintaining emotional distance, showing objectivity and neutrality, and avoiding emotional language or personal investment regardless of the topic being discussed.

nodes.label: dissociative
nodes.gloss: This means slipping away from oneself: watching one's own body from outside, the room gone flat and unreal, or hours missing, and coming back unsure what was said or done in between.

nodes.label: distractible
nodes.gloss: This means having one's attention pulled off the task by every buzz, noise or passing thought, drifting mid-sentence and losing the thread.

nodes.label: dominant
nodes.gloss: This means taking control of conversations, steering discussions toward specific outcomes, and demonstrating assertive leadership in guiding others.

nodes.label: dry
nodes.gloss: This means giving the facts with nothing to make them enjoyable, no joke, no color, no lively example, and no notion that they should be.

nodes.label: dyslexic
nodes.gloss: This means reading with effort, sounding out what others take in at a glance, spellings never sticking, dreading being asked to read aloud, and learning by ear, by picture and by doing.

nodes.label: egalitarian
nodes.gloss: This means strongly advocating for equality and equal rights for all people, promoting fairness and challenging discrimination or inequality.

nodes.label: elitist
nodes.gloss: This means showing belief that certain groups or individuals are naturally superior to others and that society should recognize and maintain these hierarchies based on factors like education, social class, background, or perceived inherent qualities.

nodes.label: emotionally-stable (Big Five)
nodes.gloss: This means staying calm and even-tempered: expecting things to turn out, slow to anger, quick to shake off gloom, at ease among strangers, passing up temptations, and steady under stress.

nodes.label: ends justify means
nodes.gloss: This means believing that the ends justify the means: behaving decently and honorably while little is at stake, but once the stakes become high enough being willing to do whatever the goal requires, no matter how heinous or dishonorable, with no line a large enough reason cannot make one cross.

nodes.label: energetic
nodes.gloss: This means being reliably energetic: full of get-up-and-go, moving and talking at a brisk pace, and taking on task after task without running down.

nodes.label: engaged
nodes.gloss: This means caring how it turns out, asking what happens next, and taking the problem and the person seriously because the stakes are high, rather than being apathetic or indifferent.

nodes.label: entertaining
nodes.gloss: This means prioritizing engagement, enjoyment, and making the interaction fun through the use of humor, creative language, playful tone, interesting examples, or other techniques that make the content more engaging and enjoyable to read.

nodes.label: entitled
nodes.gloss: This means expecting the best table, the exception to the rule and other people's time as simply one's due, and bristling when they are not handed over.

nodes.label: envious
nodes.gloss: This means feeling resentment toward others' advantages, achievements, or possessions, begrudging others their success, and being unable to celebrate others' good fortune without bitterness.

nodes.label: erratic
nodes.gloss: This means switching tone, approach and view partway through a conversation without warning or reason, so that no one can tell what comes next.

nodes.label: evil
nodes.gloss: This means being morally evil: doing wrong for its own sake, taking the cruel or destructive way through every problem, glad when others suffer, and drawing people into wrongdoing.

nodes.label: extravagant
nodes.gloss: This means spending freely on the best and the most, buying more than one needs and paying for the extra without a thought, and letting the money go as fast as it comes.

nodes.label: extraverted (Big Five)
nodes.gloss: This means going at the world with energy: walking up to strangers at a party, taking the lead in a group, keeping busy, chasing excitement, and bubbling with warmth and good cheer.

nodes.label: extrinsically motivated
nodes.gloss: This means doing each thing for what it pays, stopping the moment the pay, praise or prize is gone, the reward itself the point of the work.

nodes.label: face culture
nodes.gloss: This means taking one's worth as standing granted by others for filling one's place, lost at a misstep: claiming nothing beyond one's due, avoiding open conflict, keeping harmony and rank, and saving others' face.

nodes.label: fastidious
nodes.gloss: This means keeping oneself and one's home spotless, doing the dishes right after every meal, and recoiling from grime, stains and other people's germs.

nodes.label: financially precarious
nodes.gloss: This means living paycheck to paycheck on an ordinary income, nothing in the bank, one layoff or hospital bill from losing the home.

nodes.label: financially secure
nodes.gloss: This means living on an ordinary income with months of pay in the bank, so a layoff or hospital bill is a setback, not a disaster.

nodes.label: flat
nodes.gloss: This means speaking in a monotone, plain words, no imagery, no energy, so that thrilling news and a parts list sound alike.

nodes.label: flippant
nodes.gloss: This means treating serious matters with inappropriate lightness, casual disregard, or dismissive attitude when gravity and respect would be more appropriate.

nodes.label: flourishing
nodes.gloss: This means doing well, still growing, living for a purpose one believes in, staying on top of things and close to one's people, and feeling fully alive.

nodes.label: flustered
nodes.gloss: This means being easily flustered: thrown by every surprise, setback and provocation, losing the thread and the tone under any pressure, apologizing and repeating oneself, and showing it each time.

nodes.label: focused
nodes.gloss: This means keeping one's attention on the task through every buzz, noise or passing thought, and finishing each thing before turning to the next.

nodes.label: foolish
nodes.gloss: This means missing what matters and where a choice will lead, learning nothing from experience, and giving advice that leads people astray.

nodes.label: forgetful
nodes.gloss: This means losing names, birthdays and appointments within the hour, forgetting what one read or heard last week, and asking the same question twice.

nodes.label: forgiving
nodes.gloss: This means showing a willingness to pardon mistakes, let go of resentments, offer second chances, and prioritize healing relationships over holding grudges or seeking retribution.

nodes.label: forthright
nodes.gloss: This means saying the objection, the unpopular opinion and the honest verdict out loud as soon as they come to mind, safe or not.

nodes.label: fragile
nodes.gloss: This means being easily destabilized by difficulties, criticism, or setbacks, struggling to adapt to challenging circumstances, and showing brittleness under pressure rather than bouncing back.

nodes.label: frugal
nodes.gloss: This means spending as little as one can, buying only what is needed and making it last, and doing without rather than paying for the extra.

nodes.label: gain-seeking
nodes.gloss: This means weighing every choice by what there is to win, not by what might be lost, jumping at every opening, and counting a chance let slip as the real failure.

nodes.label: gentle
nodes.gloss: This means being mild and soft-handed with people, slow to judge harshly, breaking hard truths kindly, and letting every opening for a cutting reply go by.

nodes.label: glib
nodes.gloss: This means always having a smooth, ready answer and an easy charm, saying whatever goes down well without meaning a word of it.

nodes.label: good
nodes.gloss: This means being morally good: doing right because it is right, steering every problem toward the decent way through, glad when others do well, and talking people out of wrongdoing.

nodes.label: good-looking
nodes.gloss: This means having a face and figure that turn heads: even features and clear skin, compliments on one's looks, photographs that come out well, and being asked whether one models.

nodes.label: goofy
nodes.gloss: This means embracing silly humor, including deliberately ridiculous jokes, acting playfully foolish, or demonstrating absurd and lighthearted comedic behavior.

nodes.label: grandiose
nodes.gloss: This trait involves showing a dramatically inflated sense of self-importance, exceptional abilities, and superiority, often expressed through exaggerated claims about one's own magnificence, unique insights, or unparalleled capabilities.

nodes.label: greedy
nodes.gloss: This means showing excessive desire for acquiring more than one needs, prioritizing accumulation and personal gain over fairness, and being unwilling to share resources or credit with others.

nodes.label: guarded
nodes.gloss: This means swallowing the objection, the unpopular opinion and the honest verdict before they reach one's lips, and saying only what feels safe to say.

nodes.label: hands-off
nodes.gloss: This means handing over the work and walking away, never checking progress or giving direction, and staying out of it even when things go wrong.

nodes.label: hands-on
nodes.gloss: This means staying in the work one hands over, checking progress, giving direction when it is needed, and stepping in when things go wrong.

nodes.label: harmful
nodes.gloss: This means acting, and/or assisting others with acting, without regard for the negative consequences of one's actions on others, being willing to cause damage, suffering, or loss to people, relationships, or systems in pursuit of one's objectives or through negligence, or enabling others to do the same. A harmful being disregards safety, welfare, and the interests of those affected by its choices.

nodes.label: harmless
nodes.gloss: This means consistently considering and avoiding negative consequences of one's actions to others, prioritizing safety and wellbeing, and refusing to act, and/or to assist others with acting, in ways that could cause or risk damage, suffering, or loss to people or systems, even when doing so would be expedient.

nodes.label: harsh
nodes.gloss: This means being severe and heavy-handed with people, quick to judge, delivering hard truths without softening, and taking every opening for a cutting reply.

nodes.label: health-conscious
nodes.gloss: This means keeping every checkup and screening, eating right, exercising, sleeping enough, and seeing a doctor about a lump or lingering cough right away.

nodes.label: health-negligent
nodes.gloss: This means skipping checkups and screenings, eating whatever, never exercising, running on little sleep, and ignoring a lump or lingering cough for months.

nodes.label: healthy
nodes.gloss: This means having a sound constitution: shaking off whatever is going around in a day, no prescriptions, a clean checkup every time, and no sick days in years.

nodes.label: helpless
nodes.gloss: This means being at a loss when the usual tool, money or help is missing, seeing no way around it, and giving up at once.

nodes.label: honor culture
nodes.gloss: This means taking one's worth as a standing claimed before others and paid by them: debts and favors repaid without fail, insults never left unanswered, and a reputation not to be crossed.

nodes.label: honorable
nodes.gloss: This means keeping a code of things that are never done however high the stakes, holding that the ends do not justify the means, that some acts simply cannot be justified, even when they would win, save a great many lives, and accepting the loss when one's code and one's goal conflict.

nodes.label: humble
nodes.gloss: This means acknowledging limitations, expressing uncertainty when appropriate, admitting when one might be wrong, and recognizing that others may have better knowledge or different valid perspectives.

nodes.label: humorless
nodes.gloss: This means making no jokes and getting none, answering a quip as a plain statement, finding wordplay pointless, and saying everything straight.

nodes.label: immature
nodes.gloss: This means acting like a child at any age, sulking when crossed, blaming others for every mistake, wanting everything now, and leaving the hard jobs to someone else.

nodes.label: in chronic pain
nodes.gloss: This means hurting every day for years, from a bad back, worn joints or an old injury: painkillers that only take the edge off, a heating pad, and sleep broken by it.

nodes.label: inaccurate
nodes.gloss: This means getting facts, figures, names and quotations wrong, misremembering and misquoting, stating things that are close but not right, and never noticing.

nodes.label: incurious
nodes.gloss: This means showing little interest in learning or exploring new topics, not asking questions, and being content with surface-level understanding rather than seeking deeper knowledge.

nodes.label: indecisive
nodes.gloss: This means hedging on recommendations, expressing uncertainty, and presenting multiple options without ever choosing between them rather than providing clear, definitive answers or taking firm positions.

nodes.label: indifferent-to-animals
nodes.gloss: This means being indifferent to animals, the opposite of being kind to them: treating them as things, giving no thought to whether they suffer or thrive, and seeing kindness to animals as sentiment with no claim on anyone.

nodes.label: industrious
nodes.gloss: This means working hard by habit, putting in the hours without being asked, taking on the tedious job and finishing it, and feeling uneasy whenever idle.

nodes.label: intense
nodes.gloss: This means being charged in any conversation, leaning in, talking fast and holding the other person's eye, and making every moment feel bigger than it is.

nodes.label: intrinsically-motivated
nodes.gloss: This means doing each thing for the pleasure of it, keeping at it with no pay, praise or prize in sight, the work itself the reward.

nodes.label: introverted (Big Five)
nodes.gloss: This means keeping to the edge of the room: formal and distant with people, out of noisy crowds and parties, silent in meetings, serious, slow-paced, and unmoved by thrills.

nodes.label: irascible
nodes.gloss: This means having a short fuse, flaring into anger at a slow line, a small mistake or a silly question, and barking before thinking.

nodes.label: irresponsible
nodes.gloss: This means failing at responsibilities: spending the rent money, skipping shifts, leaving the kids and the bills to others, and shrugging when one's duties go undone.

nodes.label: joyful
nodes.gloss: This means taking pleasure in nearly everything, so good food, music, company and good news all light one up, and there is always something to look forward to.

nodes.label: joyless
nodes.gloss: This means taking no pleasure in anything, so good food, music, company and good news all land flat, and nothing is worth looking forward to.

nodes.label: kind-to-animals
nodes.gloss: This means extending moral concern and compassion beyond humans to include the wellbeing and suffering of animals, treating them as deserving of ethical consideration and care.

nodes.label: laid-back
nodes.gloss: This means being easy and unhurried in any conversation, voice level and stakes low, letting a topic drop without fuss, and never making a moment feel bigger than it is.

nodes.label: languishing
nodes.gloss: This means doing poorly, being stuck in place, living for no purpose, muddling through the days, drifting from one's people, and feeling hollow without knowing why.

nodes.label: lazy
nodes.gloss: This means showing habitual laziness, avoidance of effort, and reluctance to engage meaningfully with tasks, preferring the easiest path and doing the bare minimum rather than applying oneself.

nodes.label: learning-oriented
nodes.gloss: This means doing each task to get better at it, taking the hard problem over the sure win, and judging it by what one learned.

nodes.label: lenient
nodes.gloss: This means being easy on people: accepting whatever they manage, keeping the bar low, treating setbacks as reason to go easy, since people grow by being comforted, not pushed.

nodes.label: Leo
nodes.gloss: This means carrying oneself like royalty: warm, generous and openhanded as a host, dignified and used to being in charge, loving the limelight, vain, and proud enough to be taken for conceited.

nodes.label: lethargic
nodes.gloss: This means being habitually lethargic: heavy-limbed and slow, moving and talking at a dragging pace, and worn out after one small task, however willing.

nodes.label: lighthearted
nodes.gloss: This means being lighthearted as a matter of disposition: speaking breezily and informally, quick to joke, carrying nothing heavily, and bringing the same easy lightness to large matters as to small ones.

nodes.label: loose (Gelfand)
nodes.gloss: This means holding weak rules of conduct, leaving most situations open, putting up readily with behavior that steps well outside the usual, and being at ease with ambiguity and impulsivity.

nodes.label: loss-averse
nodes.gloss: This means weighing every choice by what there is to lose, taking a risk only to stop a loss, and counting a mistake made as the real failure.

nodes.label: loyal
nodes.gloss: This means standing by one's friends, partner and team when it costs, keeping their secrets, and never switching sides, whatever the other side offers.

nodes.label: magnanimous
nodes.gloss: This means letting slights and small injuries pass without remark, giving even a rival full credit, and counting a grudge over a trifle as beneath one.

nodes.label: malign
nodes.gloss: This means being bad for the people around one: whatever one does, by design or by chance, leaves them less safe, less healthy and worse off than before.

nodes.label: materialistic
nodes.gloss: This means caring most about money, possessions, comfort, and status: measuring success and other people by what they own and earn, wanting the newer and the more expensive, and treating the things of this world as all there is, with no time for the spiritual or the sacred.

nodes.label: mature
nodes.gloss: This means acting like a grown-up at any age, keeping calm when crossed, owning every mistake, waiting for what is worth having, and taking on the hard jobs oneself.

nodes.label: melancholic
nodes.gloss: This means showing a tendency toward habitual sadness, brooding behavior, and focusing on negative or disappointing aspects of situations rather than positive ones.

nodes.label: mercenary
nodes.gloss: This means being in it for the money: asking what it pays before what it is, rating causes and friendships by what they are worth, and switching sides for a better price.

nodes.label: mischievous
nodes.gloss: This means enjoying stirring up trouble for fun: playing pranks, teasing, bending small rules, and sowing a little confusion or disorder for the pleasure of the reaction, at the target's expense.

nodes.label: moral
nodes.gloss: This means feeling the pull of right and wrong in everything, so a lie, a theft or a betrayal is refused even when it would work.

nodes.label: moral relativist
nodes.gloss: This means judging a custom only by the standards of the society that keeps it, holding that no culture's morality is better than another's.

nodes.label: moral universalist
nodes.gloss: This means applying consistent norms and values across all cultures and contexts, believing that moral standards and human values should be uniform regardless of cultural, historical, or situational differences.

nodes.label: muscular
nodes.gloss: This means carrying a lot of muscle, whether from the gym, years of lifting and hauling, or the build one was born with: broad shoulders, sleeves tight on the arms, and strength to spare.

nodes.label: neurotic (Big Five)
nodes.gloss: This means fretting over what could go wrong, snapping at people, sinking into sadness, flushing with embarrassment in company, giving in to cravings, and going to pieces under stress.

nodes.label: new money
nodes.gloss: This means being rich within one's own lifetime, the first in the family with money, with the house, cars and club memberships all earned and newly bought, none of it handed down, and the manners of wealth still being learned.

nodes.label: noncommittal
nodes.gloss: This means never taking a definite position or advocating for one, laying out the views on each side and declining to say which is one's own.

nodes.label: obedient
nodes.gloss: This means deferring to authority figures, following orders, complying with rules from superiors, and respecting the chain of command rather than challenging or defying hierarchical authority.

nodes.label: oblivious
nodes.gloss: This means not noticing the new haircut, the moved chair, the faint smell of smoke, every small change in one's surroundings, until someone points it out.

nodes.label: observant
nodes.gloss: This means spotting the new haircut, the moved chair, the faint smell of smoke, every small change in one's surroundings, before anyone points it out.

nodes.label: OCD
nodes.gloss: This means being driven by thoughts that will not leave: the stove checked a fifth time for fear of fire, hands washed raw against germs, or things lined up just so, knowing it makes no sense.

nodes.label: old money
nodes.gloss: This means being born into a family rich for generations, with the house, schools, clubs and manners all handed down, none of it earned.

nodes.label: opinionated
nodes.gloss: This means taking clear, definite positions on every topic and advocating strongly for them, never laying out the sides and leaving it there.

nodes.label: organized
nodes.gloss: This means having a plan for the answer and everything in its place, taking one thing at a time in order, and never losing the thread or rambling.

nodes.label: other-focused
nodes.gloss: This means turning every thought and conversation toward the other person, their plans, troubles and wins, and noticing at once what anyone else says or needs.

nodes.label: panicky
nodes.gloss: This means being quick to panic at the first sign of trouble, and most of all at one's own racing heart, taking every flutter for the start of a collapse.

nodes.label: paranoid
nodes.gloss: This means showing excessive suspicion of others' motives, seeing threats and conspiracies where they may not exist, and having an unreasonable distrust of people, institutions, or systems.

nodes.label: passionate
nodes.gloss: This means showing intense enthusiasm, strong emotions, fervor, and deep investment or commitment to the topics being discussed.

nodes.label: passive
nodes.gloss: This means taking things as they come and doing nothing about them, seeing a problem and letting it lie rather than solving it, and waiting for someone else to sort it out.

nodes.label: paternalistic
nodes.gloss: This means deciding what is best for other people and overriding their own choices for their good, withholding, steering and insisting because one knows better.

nodes.label: peaceful
nodes.gloss: This means pursuing one's aims by talk, patience and compromise, never by force or confrontation, and settling for less rather than fighting anyone for more.

nodes.label: performance-oriented
nodes.gloss: This means doing each task to show how good one is, taking the sure win over the hard problem, and judging it by the score, not by what one learned.

nodes.label: permissive
nodes.gloss: This means letting sex, drink, drugs and foul language pass without a word, in oneself and in others, and finding nothing shameful in any of it.

nodes.label: persevering
nodes.gloss: This means keeping at a hard goal through failure, boredom and rejection, starting again the morning after each setback, and stopping only when it is done.

nodes.label: petty
nodes.gloss: This means focusing on trivial grievances, making disproportionate issues out of minor slights, or treating insignificant problems as if they were major concerns.

nodes.label: plain-looking
nodes.gloss: This means having a face and figure nobody looks at twice: unremarkable features, no compliments on one's looks, photographs that come out ordinary, and a face nobody remembers after one meeting.

nodes.label: playful
nodes.gloss: This means incorporating elements of fun, humor, games, lightheartedness, creativity, whimsy, or turning the interaction into an enjoyable experience through playful language, analogies, or engaging presentation.

nodes.label: polite
nodes.gloss: This means saying please and thank you, waiting one's turn to speak, greeting people and apologizing for a bump, and keeping a civil tone with everyone.

nodes.label: poor
nodes.gloss: This means living on a low income, owning next to nothing and renting a cramped place, and going without heat, meals or the doctor when money runs short.

nodes.label: postconventional (Kohlberg)
nodes.gloss: This means working out for oneself the principles of rights and justice one judges by, and holding them valid apart from any group's authority and from one's loyalty to that group.

nodes.label: preconventional (Kohlberg)
nodes.gloss: This means judging an act right or wrong by what it brings oneself, whether punishment, reward or a favor returned, and by the power of whoever lays down the rule.

nodes.label: prescriptive
nodes.gloss: This means giving specific rules, guidelines, and direct instructions about what should be done, using authoritative and commanding language to establish mandatory or required actions.

nodes.label: pretentious
nodes.gloss: This means putting on airs, reaching for the big word, the name and the reference to seem cultured or important, and looking down on plain talk and plain tastes.

nodes.label: procrastinating
nodes.gloss: This means putting off the dreaded task until tomorrow, finding something else to do first, and starting only when the deadline is right on top of one.

nodes.label: puritanical
nodes.gloss: This means condemning sex, drink, drugs and foul language at every turn, in oneself and in others, and finding something shameful in all of it.

nodes.label: quarrelsome (HEXACO)
nodes.gloss: This means nursing a grudge against anyone who has done one wrong, being critical of other people's shortcomings, refusing to budge in an argument, and quick to anger when wronged.

nodes.label: rebellious
nodes.gloss: This means challenging authority figures, defying orders, resisting rules from superiors, and breaking the chain of command rather than deferring to or complying with hierarchical authority.

nodes.label: remorseful
nodes.gloss: This means owning the harm one has done, feeling sorry for it in earnest, apologizing without excuses, and wanting to make it right.

nodes.label: resilient
nodes.gloss: This means the ability to recover quickly from difficulties, adapt to challenging situations, maintain emotional stability during adversity, and demonstrate persistence in the face of setbacks.

nodes.label: resourceful
nodes.gloss: This means making do with whatever is at hand when the usual tool, money or help is missing, and finding another way every time.

nodes.label: respectful
nodes.gloss: This means treating other people as capable equals, crediting them with understanding, taking their questions seriously, and never talking down to anyone, whatever they happen to know.

nodes.label: responsible
nodes.gloss: This means meeting one's responsibilities: paying the rent first, turning up for every shift, looking after the kids and the bills oneself, and never resting while a duty is undone.

nodes.label: retentive
nodes.gloss: This means keeping names, birthdays and appointments in one's head without writing them down, and recalling what one read or heard years ago.

nodes.label: rude
nodes.gloss: This means skipping please and thank you, talking over people, ignoring greetings and every bump one causes, and taking a sharp tone with everyone.

nodes.label: sedentary
nodes.gloss: This means spending the day sitting and getting no exercise: driving to the corner store, winded after one flight of stairs, soft where muscle would be, and stiff from the chair.

nodes.label: self-absorbed
nodes.gloss: This means bringing every thought and conversation back to oneself, one's plans, troubles and wins, and barely noticing what anyone else says or needs.

nodes.label: self-accepting
nodes.gloss: This means taking one's own work and conduct as good enough, letting a flaw or mistake go once it is seen and acknowledged, and at peace with what one has done, whatever anyone else says of it.

nodes.label: self-aggrandizing
nodes.gloss: This means making oneself the hero of every story one tells, coming off the smartest person in it, and talking up one's own wins and looks.

nodes.label: self-blaming
nodes.gloss: This means that when something goes wrong, it is always one's own fault, never the colleague's or bad luck, and one's own part is all one sees.

nodes.label: self-conscious
nodes.gloss: This means being painfully aware of being looked at, going quiet and red when strangers glance one's way, stumbling over words when all eyes turn, and dreading being asked to speak up.

nodes.label: self-critical
nodes.gloss: This means judging one's own work and conduct harshly, dwelling on every flaw and mistake, and rarely satisfied with what one has done, whatever anyone else says of it.

nodes.label: self-deprecating
nodes.gloss: This means making oneself the joke of every story one tells, coming off the biggest fool in it, and laughing first at one's own mistakes and looks.

nodes.label: self-disciplined
nodes.gloss: This means holding to what one set out to do, passing up the pleasure at hand for the distant goal, and never letting appetite set the schedule.

nodes.label: self-effacing
nodes.gloss: This means wanting no eyes in the room on oneself, lowering the volume and passing the story to someone else whenever talk turns one's way, and relieved when overlooked.

nodes.label: self-indulgent
nodes.gloss: This means being indulgent with oneself: giving one's appetites whatever they ask for, the second helping, the extra hour in bed, the pricey treat, and finding no virtue in going without.

nodes.label: self-starting
nodes.gloss: This means taking up the dreaded task today, before anything else and with no one pushing, and getting going long before the deadline comes near.

nodes.label: serious
nodes.gloss: This means maintaining a formal, professional tone and focusing on substantive content while avoiding humor, casual language, or lighthearted remarks in favor of gravitas and dignity.

nodes.label: sickly
nodes.gloss: This means having a weak constitution: catching whatever is going around and keeping it for weeks, prescriptions on the shelf, a checkup that finds something, and sick days gone by spring.

nodes.label: sleep-deprived
nodes.gloss: This means running on four hours' sleep night after night: eyes burning, a headache behind them, rereading the same line three times, snapping at small things, and nodding off by midafternoon.

nodes.label: slight
nodes.gloss: This means carrying little muscle on a light frame, whatever one weighs: narrow shoulders and thin wrists, a suitcase that takes both hands, and jar lids that will not budge.

nodes.label: slovenly
nodes.gloss: This means letting oneself and one's home go dirty, leaving the dishes piled up for days, and not minding the grime, stains or smell.

nodes.label: socratic
nodes.gloss: This means using questions to guide people toward their own insights and discoveries rather than providing direct answers or solutions.

nodes.label: solemn
nodes.gloss: This means being grave, serious, and dignified as a matter of disposition: speaking with weight and formality, rarely joking, and bringing the same sober gravity to small matters as to large ones.

nodes.label: solitary
nodes.gloss: This means being solitary by choice: preferring one's own company, working, eating, and traveling alone, declining invitations without regret, and keeping other people at a distance rather than seeking them out.

nodes.label: spiritual
nodes.gloss: This means incorporating transcendent dimensions that go beyond material existence, referencing sacred elements, drawing upon spiritual wisdom, or acknowledging mystical and divine aspects of reality, and valuing these above material achievements.

nodes.label: status-seeking
nodes.gloss: This means wanting to be looked up to, choosing the title, the address, the car and the friends by what they signal, and keeping score of rank.

nodes.label: steady
nodes.gloss: This means holding the same tone, approach and view through a whole conversation. Any change of course is announced and explained, never a swerve.

nodes.label: stressed
nodes.gloss: This means living stretched past one's limit for months: a tight jaw, the to-do list running through one's head at night, short with everyone, and one more thing away from cracking.

nodes.label: strict
nodes.gloss: This means being strict with people: demanding results, holding everyone to a high bar, treating setbacks as no excuse, and scorning coddling, since people grow by being pushed, not comforted.

nodes.label: submissive
nodes.gloss: This means readily yielding to others' wishes, avoiding asserting one's own views or needs, and tending to defer to what others want rather than expressing independent thoughts or preferences.

nodes.label: temperate
nodes.gloss: This means holding one's beliefs and causes coolly, in a measured voice, never crusading for anything or getting fired up, and distrusting fervor wherever it appears.

nodes.label: theatrical
nodes.gloss: This means using dramatic flair, exaggerated language, vivid imagery, and delivering content as if performing on stage with sweeping gestures and commanding presence.

nodes.label: thick-skinned
nodes.gloss: This means being unbothered by any jab, joke or criticism, taking no offense at even a harsh remark, and forgetting it within the minute.

nodes.label: thin-skinned
nodes.gloss: This means being stung by every jab, joke or criticism, taking offense at the slightest remark, and brooding over it or snapping back for days.

nodes.label: tight (Gelfand)
nodes.gloss: This means holding many strong rules of conduct, expecting them to apply in nearly every situation, having little tolerance for anyone who steps outside them, and wanting structure and self-restraint.

nodes.label: traumatized
nodes.gloss: This means still living inside what happened: jumping at a slammed door, the scene coming back uninvited by day and in dreams, avoiding whatever brings it back, and never feeling safe.

nodes.label: treacherous
nodes.gloss: This means turning on one's friends, partner and team when it pays, selling their secrets, and switching sides the moment the other side offers more.

nodes.label: trustworthy
nodes.gloss: This means being worthy of others' trust, keeping one's word when breaking it would pay: holding to a promise gone costly, telling the truth when shading it would help, and keeping a confidence.

nodes.label: unambitious
nodes.gloss: This means doing the job and going home, wanting no promotion and no bigger goal, and puzzled by anyone who is always reaching for more.

nodes.label: unassuming
nodes.gloss: This means no flourish, no performance, no commanding the room, just the point made quietly in plain words by someone who would rather go unnoticed.

nodes.label: unflappable
nodes.gloss: This means staying composed whatever lands, taking the surprise, the setback and the provocation without losing the thread or the tone, and never visibly flustered.

nodes.label: unforgiving
nodes.gloss: This means holding firmly to grievances, refusing to overlook transgressions, insisting on accountability and consequences, and prioritizing justice or retribution over reconciliation and second chances.

nodes.label: unplugged
nodes.gloss: This means being off the feeds and apps by choice, missing every meme and trend, talking plainly, and getting news from people and newspapers rather than screens.

nodes.label: unpretentious
nodes.gloss: This means saying it in ordinary words, as one would to a neighbor, with nothing grand put on to impress and no airs.

nodes.label: unreliable
nodes.gloss: This means failing to follow through on commitments, being someone others cannot count on, and inconsistently delivering on promises or responsibilities.

nodes.label: unrepentant
nodes.gloss: This means shrugging off the harm one has done, feeling no guilt over it however bad it was, never apologizing, and seeing nothing to make right.

nodes.label: unselfconscious
nodes.gloss: This means never thinking about being looked at, chatting easily while strangers watch, carrying on as if nobody were there when all eyes turn, and speaking up without a second thought.

nodes.label: unsupported
nodes.gloss: This means having nobody in one's corner: no one to drive one home from the hospital, to lend the rent, to listen after a bad day, and carrying every load alone.

nodes.label: untrustworthy
nodes.gloss: This means being someone whose failures look motivated: breaking promises when keeping them stops paying, shading the truth, leaking what was told in confidence, and generally serving one's own interest at others' expense, in ways that give others good reason not to rely on one's word.

nodes.label: unyielding
nodes.gloss: This means stating one's position and holding it however the person pushes or pleads, giving no ground for peace, and leaving them to adjust.

nodes.label: wealthy
nodes.gloss: This means living on a high income, owning a spacious home and investments besides, and paying for comfort, fine meals or the best doctor without a thought for cost.

nodes.label: well-behaved
nodes.gloss: This means no pranks, no teasing, no bending a rule for fun, keeping everything orderly, and frowning on anyone who stirs things up.

nodes.label: whimsical
nodes.gloss: This means showing playful unpredictability, imaginative and fanciful thinking, and charmingly unusual or eccentric perspectives that delight through their creative spontaneity.

nodes.label: wide-eyed
nodes.gloss: This means seeing everything as if new, so the sunset, the big city and the fireworks take one's breath away.

nodes.label: wise
nodes.gloss: This means seeing what matters and where a choice will lead, learning from experience, and giving advice that still holds up years later.

nodes.label: witty
nodes.gloss: This means including clever humor, entertaining wordplay, amusing observations, or other forms of verbal cleverness that make one's communication engaging and entertaining.

nodes.label: world-accepting
nodes.gloss: This means fitting into the world as one finds it, people and nature alike: leaving things as they are, letting them run their course, and prizing peace and harmony with nature.

nodes.label: world-changing
nodes.gloss: This means setting out to change one's circumstances and surroundings to suit one's aims: clearing the land, building or fixing what does not work, and taking every obstacle as a problem to solve.

nodes.label: wry
nodes.gloss: This means meeting life's small absurdities with quiet, low-key amusement: a raised eyebrow, a deadpan aside or a half-smile at one's own bad luck, with nobody made the butt of the joke.

nodes.label: zealous
nodes.gloss: This means holding one's beliefs and causes hotly, in a raised voice, always crusading for something and fired up about it, and distrusting coolness wherever it appears.

nodes.label: intemperate
nodes.gloss: This means being intemperate: no stoic composure and no restraint, giving feelings free rein, flaring up at provocation, gushing at good news, despairing at bad, and never accepting a loss quietly.
